raw_text:
Here is a concise, integrated 12-week plan for your client (36-year-old recreational lifter with a prior right medial meniscus tear). It integrates the strength program (4 days/week with upper/lower split), two knee-friendly cardio sessions per week, a nutrition plan focused on maintenance, and a structured recovery/mobility protocol. The plan is written with progression in mind, while keeping safety around the knee a core constraint (no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load, knee ROM monitored).

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 strength days per week (A/B upper, C/D lower) + 2 cardio days per week (non-consecutive when possible) + 1 weekly dedicated mobility/recovery session.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation, movement quality, baseline strength with safe ROM, gradual tendon/bone health emphasis.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload, higher total work, increased cardio volume, and greater ski-readiness load.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak strength block with ski-specific resilience, controlled fatigue, and final ski-readiness prep.
- Reps/sets/tempo: Main lifts typically 4x6–8 in Phase 2; moving toward 4–5 rep ranges in Phase 3 for peak loads. Tempo 2-0-2-0 (eccentric 2s, 0 pause, concentric 2s) for most work.

Weekly structure (typical week)
- Monday: Upper A strength
- Tuesday: Cardio 1 (knee-friendly intervals)
- Wednesday: Lower A strength
- Thursday: Upper B strength
- Friday: Rest or light mobility
- Saturday: Cardio 2 (knee-friendly intervals)
- Sunday: Lower B strength
- Mobility: 8–12 minutes daily; post-workout recovery and a weekly 20–30 minute deep-tissue/mobility session

Strength plan details (weeks 1–12)
Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4)
- Goals: Build movement quality, establish safe knee loading, baseline strength.
- Upper A
  - Main: Dumbbell floor press or bench press 3x10–12
  - Rows: Seated cable row or chest-supported row 3x10–12
  - Overhead press: DB or barbell 3x8–10
  - Lat pulldown: 3x8–10
  - Accessories: Dumbbell lateral raises 2x12–15; core carries 2x30–40m; dead bug 3x10 per side
- Lower A (knee-friendly)
  - Hip hinge: Romanian deadlift 3x8–10
  - Leg press (shallow ROM): 3x8–10
  - Split squats or shallow Bulgarian split squats: 3x6–8 per leg
  - Hamstring curl: 3x10–12
  - Glute bridge/hip thrust: 3x12–15
  - Core: curls/planks 3x30–45s
- Upper B
  - Incline press: 3x8–10
  - Cable row / low-row: 3x8–10
  - Shoulder press: 3x8–10
  - Face pulls: 3x12–15
  - Biceps/triceps: 2x10–12 each
  - Core: side planks 3x30s
- Lower B
  - Deadlift variant (safe ROM) or substitute with high-bar squat variant: 3x6–8
  - Romanian deadlift or hip hinge: 3x8–10
  - Glute bridges: 3x12–15
  - Hamstring curls: 3x10–12
  - Calf raises: 3x12–15
  - Core: dead bug variations 3x10 per side

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8)
- Goals: Progressive overload with knee-safe ranges; add accessory work; ramp cardio volume.
- Upper A
  - Bench press or floor press: 4x6–8
  - Barbell/DB row: 4x6–8
  - Overhead press: 3x6–8
  - Lat pulldown: 3x8–10
  - Face pulls: 3x12–15
  - Accessories: incline DB flys 2x10–12
- Lower A
  - RDL: 4x6–8
  - Leg press (shallow ROM): 4x8–10
  - Glute bridge/hip thrust: 4x10–12
  - Hamstring curls: 3x10–12
  - Calf raises: 4x12–15
- Upper B
  - Incline bench: 4x6–8
  - Bent-over row or low-row: 4x6–8
  - Seated/DB press: 3x6–8
  - Pull-downs: 3x8–10
  - Triceps/Biceps: 3x8–10
- Lower B
  - Deadlift variant (conventional or sumo): 4x4–6 or 4x6–8
  - Front goblet squat (shallow): 4x6–8
  - Glute bridge/hip thrust: 4x8–10
  - Leg curls: 3x8–10
  - Calf raises: 3x12–15

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12)
- Goals: Strength peak with ski-readiness focus; lower volume, higher relative intensity; maintain knee safety.
- Week 9 (consolidation)
  - Upper A: Bench 4x4–6; Barbell row 4x4–6; Overhead press 3x5–7; Lat pulldown 3x6–8; Face pulls 3x12–15
  - Lower A: RDL 4x4–6; Leg press shallow 4x6–8; Hip thrust 4x6–8; Ham curls 3x8–10; Calf raises 4x10–12
  - Upper B: Incline 4x4–6; Single-arm row 4x6–8; Seated/DB press 3x5–7; Pull-downs 3x6–8; Triceps/Biceps 3x8–10
  - Lower B: Deadlift variant 4x4–6; Front goblet squat shallow 4x6–8; Hip bridge 4x8–10; Leg curls 3x8–10; Calf raises 4x12–15
  - Cardio: optional light maintenance 20–25 minutes
- Week 10 (heavy loading)
  - Upper A: Bench 4x4–6; Pendlay row 4x4–6; Overhead press 3x4–6; Lat pulldown 3x6–8; Face pulls 3x12–15
  - Lower A: RDL 4x4–6; Leg press 4x6–8; Hip thrust 4x6–8; Ham curls 3x8–10; Calf raises 4x12–15
  - Upper B: Incline 4x4–6; T-bar row 4x4–6; Seated/DB press 3x4–6; Pull-downs 3x6–8; Triceps/Biceps 3x8–10
  - Lower B: SLDL or conventional 4x4–6; Front goblet shallow 4x6–8; Hip bridge 4x8–10; Leg curls 3x8–10
  - Cardio: optional light session
- Week 11 (peak-load microcycle 1)
  - Upper A: Bench 4x3–5; Row 4x3–5; Overhead press 3x4–6; Lat pulldown 3x6–8; Face pulls 3x12–15
  - Lower A: RDL 4x3–5; Leg press 4x6–8; Hip thrust 4x6–8; Ham curls 3x6–8; Calf raises 4x12–15
  - Upper B: Incline 4x3–5; Row 4x4–6; Seated press 3x4–6; Pull-downs 3x6–8; Triceps/Biceps 3x8–10
  - Lower B: Deadlift variant 4x3–5; Front goblet shallow 4x6–8; Hip thrust 4x8–10; Leg curls 3x8–10
  - Cardio: optional light session
- Week 12 (peak and ski prep)
  - Upper A: Bench 4x2–4; Row 4x2–4; Overhead press 3x3–5; Lat pulldown 3x6–8; Face pulls 3x12–15
  - Lower A: RDL 3x2–4; Front squat shallow 4x4; Hip thrust 3x6–8; Ham curls 3x6–8; Calf raises 4x12–15
  - Upper B: Incline 4x2–4; Row 4x2–4; Seated press 3x3–5; Pull-downs 3x6–8; Triceps/Biceps 3x8–10
  - Lower B: Deadlift variant 3x2–4; Front goblet shallow 4x4–6; Hip thrust 3x6–8; Leg curls 3x6–8; Calf raises 4x12–15
  - Conditioning: minimal or ski-simulation blocks to maintain movement patterns
- Ski-readiness criteria: symmetry, knee tolerance, ability to perform controlled turning/edge-control patterns with low pain/swelling after a light ski-run assessment.

Cardio plan (two days/week, knee-friendly, progressively engaging)
- Week 1–3: 25–40 min per session, interval and tempo mix (bike/elliptical/rower). Examples:
  - Bike: 8–12 rounds of 40s hard/60–90s easy
  - Rower: 20–30s hard/60–90s easy, 6–10 rounds
- Weeks 4–8: increased volume and density with longer intervals, circuits, and tempo blocks
  - Bike: 10 rounds x 40s hard/60s easy + 10 minutes tempo
  - Rowing/Ski-erg: 6–12 rounds of 45s hard/45s easy + 8–12 minutes tempo
  - Optional circuit day (Week 7–8): 4 stations x 45s on/15s off, 3 rounds
- Weeks 9–12: peak conditioning with controlled fatigue management
  - Maintain interval structure but reduce volume if fatigue accumulates
  - Maintain total cardio time around 40–60 minutes per session; emphasize technique and recovery

Nutrition and recovery (maintenance-focused)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, evenly distributed
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day, with higher intake around training days (especially heavier lifting and cardio)
- Fats: fill remaining calories after protein/carbs
- Peri-workout: pre-training balanced meal; post-workout protein + carbs within 1–2 hours
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 liters/day; more with cardio or in heat
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night
- Supplements: consider Vitamin D3 (1000–2000 IU), omega-3s (1–2 g/day), creatine monohydrate (3–5 g/day) if not contraindicated

Recovery and mobility plan (complements weeks 1–12)
- Daily mobility sequence: 8–12 minutes (ankle, hip, thoracic spine, knee-friendly mechanics)
- Self-myofascial release: calves, hamstrings, quads, IT band, glutes; 5–8 minutes a few times per week
- Post-workout recovery: 5–10 minutes of static stretching and light aerobic cool-down
- Weekly deep-tissue session: 20–30 minutes focusing on hips, ankles, T-spine, and knee mechanics
- Knee monitoring: mild ROM during ROM-focused work is OK; sharp pain or swelling requires scale-back
- Balance and proprioception: 2 short sessions weekly (single-leg stance on stable surface, progress to balance pad)

Return-to-sport readiness (skiing)
- A progressive, monitored plan to reintroduce ski-specific loading and turns
- Criteria: pain-free movement under load, symmetric strength and ROM, ability to tolerate anticipated ski-specific loads (deceleration, edge control, stability)
- Ski-readiness drills: controlled boot-on/off stance, band-resisted ankle dorsiflexion, and balance progression on stability surfaces

Customization options
- If you have exact equipment constraints, we can tailor exercise selections (e.g., substitute machines for free weights, adjust ROM, swap in alternate knee-friendly movements).
- If you have his current 1RM estimates, we can produce precise week-by-week loads and rest intervals for Weeks 9–12.
- If you want a printable version (calendar or one-page plan) or a CSV for planning tools, I can generate that.

Would you like me to deliver:
- A single-page client-facing summary, plus a four-page, week-by-week sheet (with sets/reps/loads and progression triggers) for Weeks 1–12?
- A separate printable training calendar with a daily checklist (including knee-pain monitoring and mobility targets)?
- A version tailored to his exact equipment (machines vs. free weights) and his current numbers (1RM estimates or initial loads)?
